newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia says maximum 6-pct GDP possible in 1998-99.
newsitem.headline: Latvia says maximum 6-pct GDP possible in 1998-99.

text.p: The Latvian finance ministry forecasts 1998-99 gross domestic product (GDP) growth at an average 3.3 percent with a maximum of six percent possible depending on various factors, officials said on Thursday.
The two scenarios depend on various factors, including the level of direct foreign investment, said Inna Shteinbuka, head of the economic analysis and fiscal policy department.
"Our base scenario shows a possible 3.3-percent rise of average annual GDP in comparative prices while the optimistic scenario has five- to six-percent annual growth," she told a news conference.
Under the slower growth scenario, foreign direct investment (FDI) was seen at one third of GDP while under the more optimistic forecast FDI was seen at three quarters of GDP.
She also said enhanced structural reform would ensure quicker economic growth and noted no large differences in forecast inflation in both scenarios.
In both scenarios, forecast inflation was estimated at about the same levels, but she said "it (inflation) will be low and will fall further with time."
The government earlier announced that it expected inflation to be 11 percent in 1997 falling to nine percent in 1998.
The government will plan a two-year budget based on these forecasts, she added.
The forecast figures in both growth scenarios are within the Maastricht criteria in terms of total state budget deficit and foreign debt, she said.
